title: Rouse paths, Wilde Lake closets, and why Howard County planned streets still sweat
headline: Rouse paths, Wilde Lake closets, and why Howard County planned streets still sweat
description: Columbia's village townhomes sit along lake paths and HOA greenways that funnel pollen into HVAC returns. Learn why planned-community ductwork loads differently — and how to keep it clear.

sections.heading: Green corridors are great for walking — and for filling returns
paragraphs: James Rouse designed Columbia around pathways, open space, and neighborhood lakes. That network of greenways means every townhome sits within a few hundred feet of mature trees, mowed turf, and standing water. All three generate airborne particulates: oak and maple pollen in spring, grass clippings through summer, and a persistent humidity blanket from lake evaporation that hangs in the air long after the sun sets.

Inside a Wilde Lake or Hickory Ridge townhome, the HVAC return grille is usually on a lower-level wall facing a sliding door or walkout. It pulls whatever drifts off the path. Pollen counts peak and then drop outdoors within days. Inside the ductwork, the same material sits on cool metal for months.

sections.heading: Mechanical closets designed for 1970s appliances
paragraphs: Most Columbia village stock went up between 1967 and the early 1990s. Furnaces were smaller, dryers vented shorter distances, and nobody expected a household to run a high-efficiency washer that spins water into a tight closet. Today the same alcove holds a taller air handler, a deeper dryer, and a vent run that kinks behind a water heater before exiting through an exterior wall.

Lint accumulates at every bend. Humid exhaust that cannot escape fast enough raises the moisture level in the closet, and that moisture migrates into the supply plenum inches away. Over time the interior surfaces of the trunk develop a tacky film that ordinary filter changes cannot reach.

sections.heading: Why the lakes matter more than most residents expect
paragraphs: Wilde Lake, Lake Kittamaqundi, and the smaller village ponds are shallow and warm through summer. They raise the relative humidity within a few blocks in a way that differs from general Mid-Atlantic mugginess. On a still July evening, dew points near lakeside townhomes can run several degrees higher than homes a mile inland along Route 108.

That extra moisture is what turns ordinary dust into a sticky coating on supply trunks. A dehumidifier in the lower level helps, but it cannot pull moisture out of sealed ductwork that already has a film inside. Cleaning removes the layer; controlling humidity afterward slows its return.

sections.heading: What Columbia village homeowners usually notice first
paragraphs: Planned-community homes tend to look well maintained from the street, so indoor air problems sneak up on owners who assume newer-looking equals cleaner. The signals worth watching:
listItems: A damp or earthy smell from the lower level each time the AC kicks on after a warm rain.
A thin yellow-green film on supply registers during April and May that reappears within a week of wiping.
Dryer loads that take noticeably longer once summer humidity sets in, even though the lint screen is clean.

sections.heading: Keeping the air path clear between professional cleanings
paragraphs: Columbia village townhomes benefit from a cleaning cycle tied to pollen season rather than a fixed calendar. After a heavy spring, the duct load is higher regardless of how recently the system was serviced. Running a lower-level dehumidifier from May through September and swapping filters every six weeks during peak pollen helps extend the interval.

When the film is already there, a professional cleaning is the reset. Scheduling details and flat-rate packages for Columbia are on the [Columbia, MD service page](/locations/columbia). Pair duct work with a [dryer vent cleaning](/dryer-vent-cleaning) if the laundry closet stays warm after a cycle finishes.

faq.a: Better filters reduce new Columbia pollen load. They do not pull film already coating cool supply trunks.
